result.title: CB-Orchestrator: Adaptive Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents via Contextual Bandits
result.comment: Presented at ICML 2026 Workshop on Compositional Learning: Safety, Interpretability, and Agents
result.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in tackling complex tasks through agentic workflows. However, manually designing these workflows is labor-intensive and lacks flexibility to adapt to diverse queries. While automated workflow optimization is a promising direction, existing methods often incur expensive API costs during training-phase feedback collection. Furthermore, they fail to adaptively reuse high-quality workflows, which creates a bottleneck for both performance and cost-effectiveness. To address these limitations, we propose CB-Orchestrator, an adaptive framework that decouples workflow generation from selection. In the first stage, we construct a diverse pool of candidate workflows via evolutionary search. In the second stage, we formulate workflow selection as a Contextual Bandit problem, which enables sample-efficient learning by balancing exploration and exploitation, thereby significantly reducing the feedback required for training. During inference, the model adaptively selects the optimal workflow tailored to each query. Evaluations across five diverse benchmarks demonstrate that CB-Orchestrator consistently outperforms all baselines. Notably, on the MATH dataset, CB-Orchestrator achieves better performance than strong recent baselines while reducing training-phase API token overhead by no less than 40.55% and total end-to-end training (including workflow pool generation) token overhead by no less than 29.73%.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CB-Orchestrator，将 LLM agent 的工作流生成与选择解耦：先用进化搜索构建候选工作流池，再把工作流选择建模为 contextual bandit 以样本高效地平衡探索与利用，推理时按查询自适应选择工作流，并在五个基准上验证并报告训练期 token 开销下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 用 contextual bandit 按查询自适应选择工作流、平衡探索与利用，可能为 LVR 中动态计算分配与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 策略选择提供方法线索，可供核查其状态与奖励定义能否迁移到 latent 推理步的取舍。
